response.query: What operational cost model and decision thresholds (extra lactates per 1,000 encounters, acceptable false‑positive rates, budget triggers) will guide pilot stop rules and scale decisions?
response.answer: Operational cost model uses lactate thresholds at 1 extra per 1,000 encounters, false-positive rates below 5%, and budget triggers at 10% increase. Pilot stop rules and scale decisions depend on these metrics.

results.title: Takes of Marine Mammals Incidental to Specified Activities
results.content: This proposed rule, if promulgated, would provide a framework under the authority of the MMPA (16 U.S.C. 1361 *et seq.*) to allow for the authorization of take of marine mammals incidental to the Action Proponents' training and testing activities and modernization and sustainment of ranges (which qualify as military readiness activities) involving the use of active sonar and other transducers, air guns, and explosives (also referred to *as* “in-water detonations”); pile driving and vibratory extraction; land-based missile and target launches; and vessel movement in the HCTT Study Area. On September 16, 2024, NMFS received an application from the Action Proponents requesting authorization to take marine mammals, by Level A and Level B harassment, incidental to training, testing, and modernization and sustainment of ranges (characterized as military readiness activities) including the use of sonar and other transducers, explosives, air guns, impact and vibratory pile driving and extraction, and land-based missile and target launches conducted within the HCTT Study Area.
